extracted.intended_audience: International Searching Authorities, Authorities specified for supplementary search, and applicants filing PCT supplementary international search requests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on procedures, timing, content and scope for Authorities conducting PCT supplementary international searches and for preparing the supplementary international search report (Form PCT/SISA/501) and related notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to be transmitted to Authority for supplementary search
rubrics_metrics.description: Once all fees and necessary additional items (translations and copies of sequence listings in electronic form) are provided, the International Bureau will transmit to the Authority specified for supplementary search a copy of each of the following: (i) the supplementary search request; (ii) the international application; (iii) any sequence listing furnished with the request for supplementary international search; (iv) any translation furnished by the applicant which is to be used as the basis of the supplementary international search; and, at the same time or promptly after their later receipt by the International Bureau: (v) the international search report and the written opinion established under Rule 43bis.1; (vi) any invitation by the International Searching Authority to pay additional fees referred to in Article 17(3)(a); and (vii) any protest by the applicant under Rule 40.2(c) and the decision thereon by the review body constituted in the framework of the International Searching Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists exact documents (items (i)–(vii)) that must be sent by the IB to the Authority specified for supplementary search to allow the supplementary search to be performed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgement of receipt of request
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of the request for supplementary international search, the Authority promptly sends an acknowledgement of receipt of the copy of the international application to the applicant and to the International Bureau using Form PCT/SISA/506.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority should promptly acknowledge receipt using the specified form (PCT/SISA/506).

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority may consider request not submitted if excluded by agreement
rubrics_metrics.description: If, whether prior to or following acknowledgement of receipt of the request for supplementary international search, the Authority finds that carrying out the search is excluded by a limitation or condition specified in the agreement between the Authority and the International Bureau, other than a limitation under Article 17(2) as applicable by virtue of Rule 45bis.5(c), the Authority considers the request not to have been submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In that case the Authority notifies the applicant and the International Bureau using Form PCT/SISA/507 and refunds the supplementary search fee to the extent specified by the agreement, using Form PCT/SISA/508 to notify the repayment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of the supplementary international search (timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority specified for supplementary search normally starts the supplementary international search promptly on receipt of the documents indicated in items (i) to (iv). However, the Authority may, at its option, delay the start of the search until it has also received the international search report and written opinion of the International Searching Authority, or until the expiration of 22 months from the priority date, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority has discretion to delay start until main ISR/written opinion is received or until 22 months from priority date; normally starts promptly when required documents received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Request for translation of written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: If the written opinion of the main International Searching Authority is not in either English or a language accepted by the Authority specified for supplementary search, the Authority may request the International Bureau to provide a translation into English, which is transmitted within two months of the date of receipt of the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure for obtaining translation of the ISA written opinion to enable consideration in supplementary search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of the request for supplementary international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may withdraw the request for supplementary international search at any time before the transmittal to the applicant of the supplementary international search report or the declaration that no such report will be established. Withdrawal shall be effective on receipt, within this time limit, of a notice addressed by the applicant to the Authority specified for supplementary search or to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notice does not reach Authority in time to prevent transmittal, the report/transmittal may still be effected; processing of the supplementary international search should stop. No general obligation for Authority to refund the supplementary search fee at this stage (IB will refund if withdrawal occurs before any documents are sent to the Authority), but Authorities may offer full or partial refunds according to internal practice; policies may be set in the Agreement under Article 16(3)(b). If notice received directly from applicant, Authority should date-stamp and promptly transmit copy to the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of the supplementary international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplementary search is performed on the basis of the international application as filed (or a translation thereof) so that it is easier for a truly complementary search to be performed and for the results to be considered together by the applicant or a designated Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even if applicant has had opportunity to file amended claims under Article 19 (or Article 34), the supplementary search is carried out on the application as filed (or translation) to ensure complementarity with the main search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirement for meaningful search
rubrics_metrics.description: If the application contains disclosure of nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences having ten or more specifically defined nucleotides or four or more specifically defined amino acids but does not contain a sequence listing complying with the relevant standard or the sequence listing furnished is not in an accepted language, the Authority may invite the applicant to furnish, within a fixed time limit, a sequence listing complying with the standard or a translation of the sequence listing in a language acceptable to it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant complies, the Authority proceeds with completion of the supplementary search on the basis of the compliant sequence listing or translation provided. Any sequence listing not contained in the international application as filed will not, subject to Article 34, form part of the international application, but will only be used as a search tool. If applicant does not comply within the time limit or response does not comply with the standard, the Authority is not required to carry out the supplementary international search to the extent that such non-compliance has the result that a meaningful search cannot be carried out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims excluded from supplementary international search — general categories
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to limitation of the supplementary international search due to a lack of unity of invention, the supplementary search may exclude: (i) any claims which would not be the subject of international search by the Authority carrying out the supplementary search, whether for reasons of clarity, subject matter or failure to provide, after a warning and opportunity to comply, a sequence listing in an appropriate form and language; (ii) where the international search report or a declaration under Article 17(2)(a) has been established before the start of the supplementary search, any claims which were not the subject of the international search; (iii) certain claims, in accordance with a limitation or condition specified in the agreement between the Authority and the International Bureau under Article 16(3)(b) (in particular limitations to the effect that supplementary international searches will not extend to any claim beyond a certain number of claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When exclusions (i) or (ii) mean that no supplementary international search report will be established, the Authority so declares and promptly notifies the applicant and the IB using Form PCT/SISA/502. If some claims are excluded but a report is established, the limitations are indicated in Box No. II of the supplementary international search report (Form PCT/SISA/501).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of matter not to be used (public order/morality/ disparaging statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Authority specified for supplementary search notes matter not to be used as defined in Rule 9.1, such as matter contrary to public order (‘ordre public’) or morality or disparaging statements which ought to be omitted from the international application as published, it suggests to the applicant, with Form PCT/SISA/511, that the applicant voluntarily correct the international application and notifies the receiving Office, the International Searching Authority and the International Bureau accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such correction must not introduce new matter. If the applicant does not make the requested corrections within the indicated time limit, the examiner proceeds with supplementary international search covering subject matter to which the claims might reasonably be expected to be directed after correction. Any correction aimed at complying with Rule 9.1 must be transmitted by the Authority to the receiving Office, the ISA and the IB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority discretion regarding Rule 48.2(l) information and suggestion to omit from publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority specified for supplementary search is not obliged to check whether the international application or other documents contain any information which appear to meet the criteria of Rule 48.2(l). If the Authority notes that the application contains information which appears to meet those criteria, it may suggest to the applicant to request the International Bureau to omit this information from international publication (using Form PCT/SISA/512).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is permissive (may suggest), not mandatory; forms for requesting omission are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access restrictions for omitted information
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the International Bureau has notified the Authority specified for supplementary search that it has omitted information from international publication or public file access, that Authority must not provide access to that information, and where applicable, to Form PCT/SISA/512, Form PCT/IB/385 and any replaced sheet submitted with Form PCT/IB/385 to any person other than the applicant or a person authorized by him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authority may provide access to any replacement sheet(s) received from the IB accompanying Form PCT/IB/385.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention — scope and absence of extra-fee opportunity
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike the case for the main international search, no opportunity is offered to pay additional fees in case it is found that the international application lacks unity of invention. Rather, the supplementary international search report is immediately established on those parts of the international application which relate to the main invention (normally the invention first mentioned in the claims).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner should consider factors in determining unity and main invention (see next metric entries). The examiner’s opinion on unity and consequent scope should be reported on the supplementary report similarly to the main search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider when determining unity of invention for supplementary search
rubrics_metrics.description: In determining whether there is unity of invention and what is considered to be the main invention the examiner should: (i) take due account of any opinion on unity of invention included in the documents indicated in items (vi) and (vii) of paragraph 15.79; (ii) consider an applicant’s specification under Rule 45bis.1(d) to limit the supplementary search to one of the inventions; (iii) where the invention first claimed would not be searched for any reason, consider the first searchable invention instead; (iv) if other inventions are easily searched, it may be appropriate to include those inventions within the scope of the supplementary search report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not bound by ISA views, the supplementary examiner should give due account to them; if applicant specified a wish to limit and examiner agrees and relevant claims not excluded, focus on that invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of examiner’s opinion on unity
rubrics_metrics.description: The normal protest procedure does not apply to requests for supplementary international search. However, the applicant may, within one month of the date of notification of the supplementary international search report, request the Authority to review the examiner’s opinion on unity of invention. This request may be subject to a review fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Results of the review are promptly notified to the applicant and copied to the IB using Form PCT/SISA/503. If the examiner’s opinion is found to be at least partly unjustified, the Authority should issue a corrected supplementary search report stating the revised view and, if appropriate, include search results for all claims which should have been included. If the opinion was entirely unjustified, the applicant should have any review fee refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent of supplementary international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum extent of a supplementary search is set out in the agreement between the International Bureau and the Authority specified for supplementary search. This may be different from the PCT minimum documentation under Rule 34 since it is expected that the main international search should cover that documentation effectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the main international search report is not received before the start of the supplementary search, the examiner may need to make assumptions about the scope which the main international search will have in order to decide the extent of the search which he should conduct. Any comments on this matter may be recorded on the supplementary international search report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for establishment of the supplementary international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplementary international search report (Form PCT/SISA/501) must be established, or declaration that no such report shall be established (Form PCT/SISA/502) must be made, within 28 months from the priority date and transmitted to the applicant and to the International Bureau using Form PCT/SISA/505.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict 28-month time limit from priority date for establishment or declaration and transmittal using specified forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of the supplementary international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The report or declaration is made in a language of publication: normally either the language of publication of the international application, or else the language of the translation provided for the purpose of the supplementary international search, though there may be cases where the first is not a language accepted by the Authority and the second is not a language of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary international search reports are drawn up in a language of publication and, if necessary, any language of publication may be used to ensure usability by applicant/third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content differences between supplementary and main international search reports
rubrics_metrics.description: The contents of the supplementary international search report are essentially the same as for the main international search report, except: (i) an indication should be given on the cover sheet whether the examiner was able to take into account the main international search report; (ii) the examiner does not classify the international application or make any indication of its classification on the supplementary international search report; (iii) it is not necessary to include the citation of any document cited in the main international search report, unless it is considered to have additional relevance when cited in conjunction with other documents not cited in the main international search report; (iv) explanation may be included regarding the citations considered to be relevant; (v) explanation may be included with regard to the scope of the supplementary international search, for example to indicate any assumptions made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary reports may include explanations (since no written opinion is established) to indicate relevant features and assumptions made by the examiner; however classification and routine duplication of main ISR citations are not required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of cited documents — access and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority must provide copies of cited documents to the applicant or any designated Office, subject to the payment of any relevant fees, on request at any time within seven years from the international filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PCT/SISA/509 may be used for requests for copies; this mirrors Article 20(3) and Rule 44.3 obligations for the ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: International search report serves as basis and must be accompanying written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The results of the international search are recorded in the international search report (Form PCT/ISA/210), which is transmitted with Form PCT/ISA/220 to the applicant and with Form PCT/ISA/219 to the International Bureau, together with the written opinion of the International Searching Authority, which must be established at the same time. The search report is published by the International Bureau and serves as a basis for the written opinion, any international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter I), and any examination by the designated Offices or by the International Preliminary Examining Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner responsible for ensuring ISR is drawn up so it can be typed/printed in final form; ISR and written opinion must be established together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for establishing the international search report (main ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search must be carried out in time to allow the final establishment of the international search report or of a declaration under Article 17(2) before the expiration of three months from the receipt of the search copy by the International Searching Authority, or nine months from the priority date, whichever time limit expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If, due to lack of unity or invitation to file a sequence listing, the time limit cannot be met, the ISR is established promptly after receipt of additional search fees or after the expiration of the time limit for payment of such fees if no payment is made, or after the receipt of the sequence listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form limitations — no matter beyond the form (main ISR), exception for supplementary explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report must contain no matter other than as required by the Form; in particular, it must contain no expressions of opinion, reasoning, arguments or explanations. However, in the case of supplementary international search reports (which are not accompanied by written opinions), the report may contain explanations with regard to the citations and the scope of the search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplementary reports are allowed to include explanatory material (items (iv) and (v) at paragraph 15.96) even though the main ISR must avoid opinions or reasoning on the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of continuation sheets and which sheets are published
rubrics_metrics.description: The printed international search report Form (PCT/ISA/210) contains two main sheets and six optional continuation sheets for necessary information: 'continuation of first sheet (1)', '(2)', '(3)'; 'continuation of second sheet'; 'patent family annex'; and 'extra sheet'. Specific continuation sheets have defined uses (e.g., continuation of first sheet (1) for sequence listing indications; (2) for unsearchable claims and/or lack of unity; (3) for abstract). Not all continuation sheets apply to supplementary or international-type searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the 'second sheet', 'continuation of second sheet' (if any), 'continuation of first sheet (2)' (if any), and 'extra sheet' (if any), and any patent family sheet will be subject of international publication; the 'first sheet' and some continuations contain information already on front page and are not published. Supplementary international search report is not included in the published international application, but the complete document is made available to the public, with English translation where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cases where no or limited search report is established — subject-matter exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: No International Searching Authority is required to search or examine an international application to the extent that its subject matter is: (i) scientific and mathematical theories, (ii) plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for production of plants and animals (other than microbiological processes and products thereof), (iii) schemes, rules or methods of doing business, performing purely mental acts or playing games, (iv) methods for treatment of the human or animal body by surgery or therapy, as well as diagnostic methods, (v) mere presentations of information, (vi) computer programs to the extent that the ISA is not equipped to search prior art concerning such programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chapter 9 deals with these exclusions in detail as well as other situations (lack of clarity) where it may not be possible to establish a meaningful search in respect of some or all claims; supplementary international search reports may also exclude claims which were not the subject of the main international search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction of the subject of the international search — categories and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The report indicates whether the search was restricted or not for any of four categories: (i) claims drawn to subject matter not required to be searched by the International Authority; (ii) claims in respect of which a meaningful search cannot be carried out; (iii) multiple dependent claims which do not comply with Rule 6.4(a); (iv) lack of unity of invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claims are not searched for reasons (i)–(iii) box 2 of the first sheet is checked and Box No. II is completed giving details. For lack of unity box 3 is checked and Box No. III is completed indicating separate inventions, whether additional fees were requested/paid, which claims were searched, and whether any fees were protested. For supplementary searches, no opportunity to pay additional fees — only a single invention is searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omnibus claims and reporting of breaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims which rely, in respect of the technical features of the invention, on references to the description or drawings ('omnibus claims') are searched and reported upon if they can be given a definite construction. However, in the written opinion and for international preliminary examination, any breach of Rule 6.2(a) (no reference to the description or drawings except when absolutely necessary) may be reported in Box No. VII of the opinion or report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the national law of the Office acting as ISA permits multiple dependent claims non-compliant with Rule 6.4(a), such claims are included in the international search and no indication is made under item 3 of Box No. II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title, abstract and figure approval/amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must contain a title and an abstract. The examiner conducting the main international search indicates approval or amendment of the title of the invention, the text of the abstract, and the selection of the figure that is to accompany the abstract in items 4 to 6 of the first sheet of the international search report. Box No. IV ('continuation of first sheet (3)') is used to record any new or amended abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuation sheet usage and where to record amendments to title/abstract/figure are specified.
